2027-03-06.title: Saturday of the Third Week of Lent
readings: I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings
It is mercy I desire, and not sacrifice
The tax collector went home justified rather than the Pharisee
2027-03-06.alt: Lenten weekday. The Alleluia is omitted throughout Lent; the Gloria is omitted except on solemnities and feasts. Liturgical colour: violet. On any weekday of this third week, especially where there are catechumens, the Mass of the Samaritan woman may be used instead: Exodus 17:1–7; Psalm 95; John 4:5–42.
2027-03-06.verse: But the tax collector, standing far off, would not even look up to heaven, but was beating his breast and saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’
theo: The first reading opens with a beautiful song of repentance: “Come, let us return to the LORD; for it is he who has torn, and he will heal us… After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up.” The Fathers of the Church heard in these words a hidden promise of the Resurrection on the third day. But God's reply is sobering: “What shall I do with you, O Ephraim?… Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early.” The people's repentance is sincere for an hour and then evaporates in the sun. God wants something deeper and more lasting: “For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.” The Hebrew word for steadfast love, hesed, means faithful, covenant love, the kind that does not dry up by noon. Jesus himself quoted this verse twice when he was criticized for eating with sinners: “Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’” The Psalm, David's great prayer of repentance, gives us the words: “The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”

In the Gospel two men go up to the Temple to pray. The Pharisee stands by himself and gives thanks, but only for himself: “God, I thank you that I am not like other people: thieves, rogues, adulterers, or even like this tax collector. I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all my income.” Everything he says is true. He really fasts and really gives. But he has come to God to be admired, and he looks down on his neighbour. The tax collector, a man despised as a collaborator with Rome, stands far off, will not lift his eyes, beats his breast, and says only: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” Jesus says this man “went down to his home justified rather than the other.” The parable is told, Luke says, “to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and regarded others with contempt.” It is a warning to every devout person, especially in Lent, when our fasting and almsgiving can quietly become a mirror. The tax collector's prayer has become one of the treasures of the Church: the Jesus Prayer of the East, “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner,” grew from it, and at every Mass we strike our breast with him at the Confiteor. On this Saturday before Laetare Sunday, it is a good day to go to confession and to pray his prayer.
outline: Ask: when you pray, do you compare yourself with others?
Point 1 · Love like a morning cloud
Point 3 · Two men went up to pray
Point 4 · God, be merciful to me
“All who humble themselves will be exalted.”
live: Repeat slowly today, with your breathing: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
Each time you catch yourself judging someone today, say a blessing for them instead.
2027-03-06.prayer: Merciful God, you desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, and you do not despise a broken and contrite heart. Free us from pride and from contempt for others; make our love faithful and not like the morning dew; and let us go down to our homes justified, praying with the tax collector: God, be merciful to me, a sinner. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Before we approach the altar we strike our breast and say: through my fault. At the Lamb of God we confess: Lord, I am not worthy. Like the tax collector, we come to the Eucharist as sinners who trust in mercy, and we go home justified.

quick: Hosea warns that our love can vanish like morning dew; God desires steadfast love, not sacrifice.
The Pharisee prayed about himself and despised others.
The tax collector prayed, “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” and went home justified.
2027-03-06.action: Go to confession today or this weekend, and pray the tax collector's prayer often.
2027-03-06.question: In my prayer and my Lenten practices, am I seeking God's mercy or my own admiration?

family.explain: Two men went to God's house to pray. One said: God, I am better than everyone else! The other said: God, I am a sinner, please be kind to me. Jesus said the second man was the one God was happy with, because he was humble and honest.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to say sorry.
family.ask: Ask: “Can each of us say the humble man's prayer together tonight before bed?”

illus: In a parish in Ernakulam the church committee had two very different members. One kept careful accounts of everything he gave and mentioned it at every meeting. The other, a fisherman who had once been in jail, always sat at the back and said little. When the old parish priest was dying, he asked for the fisherman to come and pray with him. Asked why, he whispered: because he prays like the tax collector. When he asks for mercy, heaven listens.

pm.open: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Amen.
share: Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early (Hosea 6:4). Where has my repentance faded?
For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice (Hosea 6:6). What does God really want from me this Lent?
God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13). Can I pray this without adding any excuses?
pm.resp: It is mercy I desire, and not sacrifice.
interc: For all who will go to confession this weekend, that they may experience God's mercy.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be faces of the Father's mercy.
For those who despise others, that God may give them humble hearts.
For those who think they are too sinful to pray, that they may find courage in the tax collector.
For our group, that our Lenten practices may be humble and hidden.
pm.close: Father, you raise up the humble and receive the contrite. Make our love steadfast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the people in Hosea sing: come, let us return to the LORD; for it is he who has torn, and he will heal us (Hosea 6:1). It sounds like a perfect repentance. But God answers: your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early (Hosea 6:4). Their conversion lasted an hour.

God wants more: for I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings (Hosea 6:6). Faithful love, not religious display. Jesus repeated these words when people complained that he ate with sinners.

In the Gospel two men pray in the Temple. The Pharisee says: God, I thank you that I am not like other people… I fast twice a week; I give a tenth of all my income (Luke 18:11–12). What he says is true, but he prays to a mirror. The tax collector stands far off, beats his breast, and says: God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13).

Jesus says the tax collector went down to his home justified, for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted (Luke 18:14). This weekend, let us bring that prayer to the confessional. God does not despise a broken and contrite heart. Amen.
kids: Children, two men prayed in church. One said: God, I am better than everybody! The other said: God, I am sorry, please be kind to me. God loved the humble prayer. Let us say tonight: Jesus, I am sorry, please be kind to me.

intro: Theme: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!”
Love like the morning dew, the steadfast love God desires, and the prayer that justifies.

sub: On the third day he will raise us up.
q: What shall I do with you, O Ephraim? What shall I do with you, O Judah? Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early.
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Choose one Lenten resolution that has faded since Ash Wednesday and begin it again today.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
Go and learn what this means, ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.
points.apply: Do one act of mercy this weekend for someone others look down on.

q: For thus says the high and lofty one who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: I dwell in the high and holy place, and also with those who are contrite and humble in spirit,
I tell you, this man went down to his home justified rather than the other; for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: Go to confession this weekend, and begin with the tax collector's words.

concl: God desires faithful love, not display.
The humble prayer of a sinner is heard, and he goes home justified.
2027-03-06.resolve: Pray the Jesus Prayer several times each day until Easter.
